deities: Rishi Markandeya (sage; idol depicts him as an eternally youthful clean-shaven youth)
festivals: Baisakhi fair (annual religious fair at the temple)

history.summary: Markandeya Ji Temple, at Markand (Makari Markandeya / Markand Makri village, ~20 km from Bilaspur on the Ghagus-Brahmpukhar road), is named for sage Rishi Markandeya, disciple of Rishi Ved Vyas and one of the seven chiranjivis. Legend says Rishi Mrikandu was blessed by Lord Shiva with a son fated to die at twelve; the boy Markandeya worshipped Shiva here, gained immortality (tradition says on Baisakhi), and a holy spring broke out at the spot. The spring is said to cure infertility and infant diseases; childless couples apply kajal to one eye of the idol and vow to apply it to the other after a child is born. A folk-lore account connects a Vyas cave here (marked 'Vyas gupha') as the far end of a tunnel from the Bilaspur Vyas Gufa. The fair held on Baisakhi draws the largest crowds. Note: one travel page mislabels this site as a Kullu/Shiva temple — the Bilaspur Markandeya Ji shrine is a sage shrine, not a Shiva temple (verify).

name: Markandeya Ji Temple
town_description: Markand (also called Maakdi or Makari Markandeya) is a village in Bilaspur district of Himachal Pradesh, about 20 km from Bilaspur town on the Ghagus-Brahmpukhar road. It is known primarily for the Markandeya Ji temple and its holy spring. The surrounding landscape is hilly and forested, typical of the lower Shivalik region.
